items.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Yeah. Like Ramsey Lewis was playing rock. You know? ... [INTERVIEWEE] The man was a hell of a pianist.

ctx.x: so good and knew the rhythms. That’s the important thing. He knew those rhythms and he would play them and play them comfortable. So if they asked for a rock tune, what I would do, I had some blues/rock things with the background, and I would play them. “Oh yeah, you played rock.” I said, “Yeah, we play rock.”
Yeah. Like Ramsey Lewis was playing rock. You know? He just took songs and sort of put a rock beat to it.

The man was a hell of a pianist. Yeah. There’s really nothing difficult, but the main thing is the rhythm. If you’re a pianist or you are a drummer or a bass player and you have that rhythm in your mind, you feel it you know, you can play it. Because it’s music, it’s compatible music. When you figure it all out it’s music.
